He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State Buckeyes]]. His father is former NBA player [[Duane Washington]]. ==Early life== Washington was born in [[Frankfurt]], Germany, while his father was playing for [[Skyliners Frankfurt]].{{Cite web|date=August 17, 2017|title=Reclaiming a name: the trials of two Duane Washingtons|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/85507/2017/08/17/reclaiming-a-name-the-trials-of-two-duane-washingtons/|last=Quinn|first=Brendan|website=[[The Athletic]]}} Washington was raised in [[Grand Rapids, Michigan]], and went to high school for his first three years at [[Grand Rapids Christian High School]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/sports/grand-rapids/2017/07/whats_making_gr_christians_dua.html|first=Peter|last=Wallner|title=What makes Grand Rapids Christian's Duane Washington Jr. a hot recruit?|website=MLive|date=20 July 2017 }} He averaged 13.1 points and 4.5 assists as a junior.{{Cite web|url=https://ohiostatebuckeyes.com/roster/duane-washington-jr/|title=Duane Washington Jr. - Ohio State Men's Basketball|website=Ohio State Athletics|date=9 July 2018 }} Washington transferred to [[Sierra Canyon School]] in [[Los Angeles]] before his senior season of high school. He transferred to go to live with his uncle Derek Fisher, and learn from the 5-Time NBA Champion.{{Cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/highschoolsports/article/michigan-recruit-duane-washington-of-grand-rapids-christian-transferring-to-california-school/|first=Steve|last=Kaminski|title=Michigan recruit Duane Washington of Grand Rapids Christian transferring to California school|website=MLive|date=9 August 2017 }} During his time at Sierra Canyon, he played with [[Scotty Pippen Jr.]], [[Cassius Stanley]], and [[Kenyon Martin Jr.]]{{Cite web|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/high-schools/sierra-canyon-trailblazers-(chatsworth,ca)/basketball-winter-17-18/roster.htm|title=Roster - Sierra Canyon (2017–2018)|website=MaxPreps}} He averaged 15.5 points per game, 4.5 rebounds per game, and 3.8 assists per game as a senior. Washington was considered a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[ESPN]] and a three-star recruit by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]] and [[Rivals.com|Rivals]]. On September 20, 2017, Washington committed to play college basketball for [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] over offers from teams such as [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]], [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], and [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]].{{Cite (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|Washington with [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] in 2020]] In Washington's second game at [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] against [[2018–19 Purdue Fort Wayne Mastodons men's basketball team|Purdue Fort Wayne]], Washington scored 20 points in 21 minutes off the bench.{{Cite web|url=https://www.dailyastorian.com/sports/national/second-half-burst-helps-buckeyes-rout-purdue-fort-wayne/article_b6c357dd-eb2a-5c99-93bf-337ecebc8570.html|title=Second-half burst helps Buckeyes rout Purdue Fort Wayne|website=Daily Astorian|date=November 11, 2018 }} For the year, he played in 35 games, starting two of them. He averaged 7 points per game, 2.5 rebounds per game, and 17.2 minutes per game. During his sophomore year, Washington scored 20 points in a game two times, matching his career{{endash}}high at the time.{{Cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2020/03/01/no-23-buckeyes-surge-late-to-beat-no-19-michigan-77-63/111388482/|title=No. 23 Buckeyes surge late to beat No. 19 Michigan 77-63|website=USA Today}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.dispatch.com/sports/20200118/ohio-statersquos-duane-washington-jr-addresses-suspension-loss-at-penn-state|title=Duane Washington Jr addresses suspension after loss at Penn State|website=Columbus Dispatch|access-date=January 18, 2021|archive-date=January 22, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210122130645/https://www.dispatch.com/sports/20200118/ohio-statersquos-duane-washington-jr-addresses-suspension-loss-at-penn-state|url-status=dead}} He, along with [[small forward]] Luther Muhammad, were suspended for the [[2019–20 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Nebraska]] game on January 14, 2019, for "failure to meet program standards". In total, he played in 28 games and started 15 of them. He averaged 11.5 points per game, which ranked second on the team. Washington scored a career{{endash}}high 30 points in an 87–92 loss against [[2020–21 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]] during his junior season.{{Cite web|url=https://www.10tv.com/article/sports/ohio-state-michigan-basketball-feb-21-2021/530-9f70f8f0-1130-4e28-ba8e-2a525254b28b|title=No. 4 Ohio State falls to No. 3 Michigan 92-87|website=10WBNS|date=21 February 2021 }} In the final seconds of Ohio State's overtime [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2021 NCAA tournament]] first-round matchup against [[2020–21 Oral Roberts Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Oral Roberts]], Washington missed what would've been a buzzer{{endash}}beating three{{endash}}pointer to tie the game and force double{{endash}}overtime.{{cite web|url=https://www.buckeyextra.com/story/mens-basketball/2021/03/19/ohio-state-exits-ncaa-tournament-stunning-loss-oral-roberts/4758812001/|first=Adam|last=Jardy|title=Stunned: Ohio State falls to No. 15 seed Oral Roberts in NCAA Tournament|website=BuckeyeXtra}} Washington averaged 16.4 points, 3.4 rebounds, and 2.9 assists per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/duane-washingtonjr-1.html|title=Duane Washington Jr. College Statistics|website=Sports Reference}} On March 31, 2021, Washington declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while initially maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/ohiostate/basketball/ohio-state-basketball-guard-duane-washington-jr-delcares-for-nba-draft|first=Brendan|last=Gulick|title=Duane Washington Jr. Declares for 2021 in NBA draft, won't return to Ohio State for senior season |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31734745/duane-washington-jr-staying-nba-draft-return-ohio-state-senior-season |access-date=July 1, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=June 29, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Indiana Pacers (2021–2022)=== [[File:Duane Washington Jr..jpg|thumb|right|Washington with the Pacers in 2022]] After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Washington signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Indiana Pacers]] on August 5, 2021, splitting time with their G League affiliate, the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]].{{cite web|title=Pacers Sign Washington Jr., Sykes, Taylor|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-washington-jr-sykes-taylor|website=NBA.com|date=August 5, 2021|access-date=August 14, 2021}} On January 24, 2022, Washington scored a team-high 21 points, knocking down seven [[Three-point field goal|3-pointers]], setting a franchise record for most threes by a rookie while becoming the 36th rookie in the league history to hit seven threes in a game.{{cite tweet|author=Wheat Hotchkiss|number=1485816490439884804|title=Per Pacers PR, Duane Washington Jr.'s seven 3-pointers tonight are a team rookie record. Chuck Person and Chris Duarte each had a game with six threes.|user=Wheat_Hotchkiss|access-date=January 24, 2022}}{{cite tweet|author=Tony East|number=1485816537747439618|title=Duane Washington is the 36th rookie in NBA history to hit 7 threes in a game.|user=TEastNBA|access-date=January 24, 2022}} On April 7, the Pacers converted his two-way contract into a standard one.{{cite web|title=Pacers Sign Terry Taylor And Duane Washington, Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-taylor-washington-jr|website=NBA.com|date=April 7, 2022|access-date=April 7, 2022}} On July 14, 2022, Washington was waived by the Pacers.{{cite web | url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-waive-four-players-2 | title=Pacers Waive Four Players | website=[[NBA.com]] }} ===Phoenix Suns (2022–2023)=== On August 3, 2022, Washington signed a two-way contract with the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web |title=Suns sign Duane Washington Jr. |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-sign-duane-washington-jr |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 1, 2023 |date=August 3, 2022}}{{cite web |last1=Anderson |first1=Jake |title=Phoenix Suns sign guard Duane Washington Jr. to 2-way contract |url=https://arizonasports.com/story/3239196/phoenix-suns-sign-guard-duane-washington-to-2-way-contract/ |website=Arizona Sports |access-date=March 1, 2023 |date=August 3, 2022}} On December 27, he scored a career-high 26 points, alongside four rebounds and eight assists, in a 125–108 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web |title=Washington scores 26 as banged-up Suns beat Grizzlies |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468665 |website=ESPN |access-date=March 1, 2023 |date=December 27, 2022}} On February 1, 2023, Washington was waived |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2023/02/02/phoenix-suns-sign-saben-lee-to-two-way-waive-duane-washington-jr/69864611007/ |website=The Arizona Republic |access-date=March 1, 2023 |date=February 1, 2023}} ===Westchester Knicks (2023–2024)=== On February 28, 2023, Washington signed a two-way contract with the [[New York Knicks]],{{cite web|title=Knicks Sign Duane Washington Jr. to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/knicks-sign-duane-washington-jr-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=February 28, 2023|access-date=March 1, 2023}} but was waived on July 24.{{cite web|first=Alex|last=Kirschenbaum|title=Duane Washington Cut By Knicks|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/07/duane-washington-cut-by-knicks.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=July 24, 2023|access-date=July 30, 2023}} Six days later, he re-signed with the Knicks,{{cite web|title=Knicks Sign Duane Washington Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/knicks-sign-duane-washington-jr|website=NBA.com|date=July 30, 2023|access-date=July 30, 2023}} but was waived on October 21.{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=Knicks waive Mamadi Diakite, Brandon Goodwin, Isaiah Roby and Duane Washington Jr.|number=1715832489313182178|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=October 22, 2023}} Three days later, he signed another two-way contract,{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=Knicks sign Duane Washington Jr.|number=1716886327462146288|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=October 29, 2023}} but was waived again on November 27.{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=Knicks waive Duane Washington Jr.|number=1729233663920115769|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=November 27, 2023|access-date=November 28, 2023}} On January 3, 2024, Washington signed another two-way contract with New York, joining the team for the 2024 playoffs, however did not make an appearance.{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=Knicks sign Duane Washington Jr. to two-way contract|number=1742667496241389678|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=January 3, 2024|access-date=January 4, 2024}} ===Partizan (2024–2026)=== On August 20, 2024, Washington signed with [[KK Partizan|Partizan Mozzart Bet]] of the [[ABA League]], [[Basketball League of Serbia]] (KLS) and the [[EuroLeague]].{{cite web|title=Crno-bela simfonija: Nova energija i duh tradicije Partizana na ulasku u sezonu 2024-25|url=https://partizan.basketball/vesti/aktuelno/3738|website=Partizan.basketball|date=August 20, 2024|access-date=August 20, 2024|language=Serbian}}{{cite web|first=Frankie|last=Sachs|title=Partizan plugs in combo-guard Duane Washington|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/kk-partizan-plugs-in-combo-guard-duane-washington/|website=EuroLeagueBasketball.net|date=August 19, 2024|access-date=August 19, 2024}} He appeared in two [[ABA League]] games, averaging 6.5 points in 8.5 minutes of playing time.{{cite web|title=Duane Washington > Player : AdmiralBet ABA League|url=https://www.aba-liga.com/player/4806/24/1/duane-washington/|website=ABA-Liga.com|access-date=October 2, 2024}} On October 2, 2024, Washington was signed by the [[New York Knicks]] and then traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in a three team trade also involving the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. The Timberwolves acquired [[Keita Bates-Diop]], [[Donte DiVincenzo]], [[Julius Randle]], and one lottery protected first-round pick; the Hornets also received [[Charlie Brown Jr. (basketball)|Charlie Brown Jr.]], [[DaQuan Jeffries]], three second-round picks and draft compensation while the Knicks acquired [[Karl-Anthony Towns]] and the draft rights to [[James Nnaji]].{{cite web|title=Hornets Acquire Three Picks, Three Players In Three-Team Trade|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-acquire-three-picks-three-players-in-three-team-trade|website=NBA.com|date=October 2, 2024|access-date=October 2, 2024}} However, he was waived on October 9{{cite web|title=Hornets Waive Duane Washington Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-waive-duane-washington-jr|website=NBA.com|date=October 9, 2024|access-date=October 9, 2024}} and five days later, he rejoined [[KK Partizan|Partizan]].{{cite web|first=Johnny|last=Askounis|title=Duane Washington Jr. completes unique path back to Partizan|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1727967/duane-washington-jr-returns-to-partizan-euroleague/|website=EuroHoops.net|date=October 14, 2024|access-date=October 14, 2024}} In his debut season with Partizan, he averaged 7.6 points and 1.7 rebounds over 19 EuroLeague games, while shooting 38.2% from the field. During the 2024–25 season, Partizan managed to lift the record eighth [[2024–25 ABA League First Division|ABA League]] championship, and the [[2024–25 Basketball League of Serbia|Serbian League]] championship, the first one after 11 seasons. For his performances during the Serbian League playoffs, Washington was named the top scorer and the [[BLS Playoff MVP|Playoff MVP]]. On December 22, 2025, in a 99–92 road win over [[KK Krka|Krka]], Washington broke the [[ABA League]] record for most points scored in a single game with 48 points on 16-of-24 shooting, including 10 made three-pointers.[https://www.eurohoops.net/en/aba/1910734/washington-scores-48-and-partizan-completes-the-comeback-in-slovenia/ Duane Washington scores 48 for a new all-time ABA League record] On June 12, 2026, following Partizan's Game 4 loss to [[Dubai Basketball]] in the [[ABA League]] Finals, Washington announced that he was leaving the club. One hour later, Partizan officially confirmed his departure through its social media channels.{{cite news|title=Partizan guard confirms his departure from Belgrade|url=https://basketnews.com/news-249633-partizan-guard-confirms-his-departure-from-belgrade.html|work=BasketNews|date=June 12, 2026|access-date=June 13, 2026 }} ===Bayern Munich (2026–present)=== On July 3, 2026, Washington signed a two–year deal with [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL).{{cite web|title=A shooter for up-tempo basketball: Bayern signs Duane Washington Jr.|url=https://fcbayern.com/basketball/en/news/2026-27/07/signing-duane-washington-jr|website=fcbayern.com|date=July 3, 2026|access-date=July 2, 2026}}
